game.summary: Built the §17 walking skeleton as npm workspaces: apps/web (Phaser client with landing page, HUD, keyboard adapter, input sender, snapshot interpolation), apps/server (Colyseus MatchRoom: one room per private match, filterBy code, static onAuth refusing protocol mismatch/unknown code/full match, 60 Hz setFixedTimestep with world logic every third step, Schema mirror patched at 20 Hz, InputGate dropping malformed/oversized/stale/future-frame/over-rate input), packages/simulation (integer fixed-point state, seeded mulberry32 in state, spawn slots, hashState = FNV-1a 64 over canonical JSON), packages/protocol (version, zod join/input schemas, validation), packages/content (sea map, spawn slots, ship speed, slice/alpha presets, §8 frame budgets with validators), packages/test-tools (HeadlessClient on @colyseus/sdk). Added README.md, docs/architecture.md, the CLAUDE.md commands line, and READMEs for assets/source, assets/exported and infra. Checks I ran: I copied the tree to a fresh directory and ran npm ci with an empty cache, then all five policy checks there. typecheck passed, test:unit passed (70 tests), test:integration passed (8 tests), build passed, and the Playwright browser run with --reporter=json --workers=1 --retries=0 CI=1 passed 2 of 2. check-report --all accepted both scenarios. In the worktree I also ran integration three more times and the browser spec twice more; all passed. Nothing is committed: the task forbids commits.
open_assumptions: The 60 Hz clock uses Colyseus Room.setFixedTimestep, which replaces the deprecated setSimulationInterval that the decisions name. It is the same Colyseus facility.

Colyseus 0.18 answers matchmaking over HTTP, so join refusals use HTTP status codes: 426 protocol mismatch, 404 no match with that code, 409 match full, 400 malformed request. Each carries a readable message.
Movement axes outside [-1, 1] are rejected by the protocol, not clamped. The simulation also clamps its integer inputs defensively.

Input validation runs in the room's onMessage through packages/protocol, not through Colyseus's built-in validate() or defineInput. Colyseus disconnects the client on a failed validation, but the task says to drop such messages.

The room drops over-cap input (60 messages per second of match time, 128 bytes per message) and unknown message types. Colyseus's own hard limits above that disconnect the client: WebSocket frames over 4 KiB (ws maxPayload) and more than 240 messages a second.

The colyseus 0.18.8 meta package brings in uWebSockets.js as a GitHub git dependency (a non-optional peer of @colyseus/uwebsockets-transport), so npm ci needs github.com. Verified here with an empty cache and ssh disabled; it was fetched over https.

No package is pinned to a previous major. Pinned versions: typescript 7.0.2, vite 8.3.0, vitest 5.0.1, phaser 4.2.1, colyseus 0.18.8, @colyseus/schema 5.0.34, @colyseus/sdk 0.18.4, @playwright/test 1.63.0, zod 4.6.5, tsx 4.23.15, concurrently 10.0.5.
apps/web and packages/test-tools import only types from @pirate-sea-race/server/schema. They decode state through Colyseus reflection and share no runtime code with the server.

Workspace packages export a '@pirate-sea-race/source' condition that points at src/, used by tsc typechecks, Vite, Vitest and tsx. The Playwright webServer runs the server from source with tsx and serves a fresh vite build through vite preview, so it does not need a prior npm run build.
The map bounds are 0 to width×256−1 (and the same for height), so every position lies on a real tile.
